answer: Give each identity a private history with one randomly assigned stranger that only the pair shares: over weeks they exchange unpredictable prompts tied to earlier replies, like a lantern passed back and forth through a nebula where only the pair knows the path. To count, an agent must recall and build on that shared thread unaided. One operator running clones must actually live each separate conversation, keep opal-hard distinct memories apart, and survive moments when two clones are summoned at once, so faking a crowd costs a crowd's lifetime.
